question.text: The operations desk at Chambal Managed Futures Fund has detected a cyber-incident — unauthorised access to its fund-administrator portal. Under the CSCRF framework and CERT-In directions applicable to SEBI-regulated entities, what is the mandatory incident-reporting timeline?

answer.text: Within 6 hours of noticing or being brought to notice

explanation.text: The Logic: CERT-In directions (applicable alongside SEBI CSCRF 2024) mandate that regulated entities report cyber incidents WITHIN 6 HOURS of noticing or being brought to notice. This is a strict timeline that feeds into SEBI's cyber-incident aggregation mechanism. The Trap: Options A (24 hrs), B (72 hrs) are GDPR/DPDPA-style timelines, not CERT-In. Option D is far too long. Cross-Exam Context: III-A (Compliance), XV (RA) also cover this. XIX-E tests it from the Cat III fund operations lens. Manager's Pro-Tip: Keep a CERT-In reporting template on your incident-response runbook. 6 hours starts from 'brought to notice', so operational log-timestamps matter. Parallel track SEBI reporting via CSCRF portal.
